Wikivoyage guide for Nuwara Eliya (all topics):
[Introduction] Nuwara Eliya (pronounced nu-REL-iya) is a city in the Hill Country of Sri Lanka. At 1,868 m (6,129 ft) altitude, the architecture and temperate climate gives it a very different feel from the rest of the country.
[Understand] The city was founded by British explorer Samuel Baker in 1846. Nuwara Eliya (which literally means 'city of lights') was built as a hill country retreat where the British colonialists could immerse themselves in pastimes such as fox hunting, deer hunting, elephant hunting, polo, golf and cricket. ...
[Get in] By train: Seven times daily there are trains coming from Colombo or Kandy, and they then proceed further to Badulla. The journey between Kandy and Ella is considered one of the most spectacular in the world. Book tickets well in advance, because unreserved coaches get crowded. There are 4 trains per day from Kandy, 4-5½ hours, 2nd class Rs 1200, 1st class/observation saloon Rs 2000. ...
[Get around] The town centre is small enough to walk around. To visit sites further afield, take a bus or hire a three-wheeler. A tuktuk within town (e.g. from city center to Pedro Tea Factory) should cost around Rs 700 (2024). The same caveat applies to touring around the area as for getting there. Assume that you'll not exceed 20 km/h no matter what the mode of (ground) transport. ...
[See] 1 Victoria Park. A pleasant place to spend an hour or so, with an astonishing variety of plants, ranging from tropical rain forest to English country garden. At the far southern end of it there is Victoria Museum which houses a collection of old colonial era photos, entrance fee is included into Victoria Park's entrance ticket. Rs1000 (kids 500). (updated May 2025) 2 Nuwara Eliya Post Office. ...
[Do] Take a walk up through the tea plantations south-west of the town to the top of Single Tree Hill for a splendid view over Nuwara Eliya. From the hill top you can walk north for a couple of kilometres along the ridgetop to a nearby village and get a tuk-tuk/three-wheeler or walk back to town. Playing golf is also an option at 1 Nuwara Eliya Golf, along with heading to the 2 racecourses (the only proper ones in Sri Lanka). ...
[Sleep] Budget: Blue Moon Guest House, Ranasinghe Mawatha. Guest house with 4 bedrooms, dining area, and common sitting area. Friendly staff. US$15-20. Mid-range: Mount View Cottage (is a small guesthouses with 4 rooms. Clean accommodation and is operated by honest people. They will arrange tours to Horton's Plains using the guesthouse's van for a reasonable amount of money (see section above). From US$50/57. ...
Not covered by this article: safety and health. Do not fill this in.

Wikivoyage guide for Nuwara Eliya (see and do):
[See] 1 Victoria Park. A pleasant place to spend an hour or so, with an astonishing variety of plants, ranging from tropical rain forest to English country garden. At the far southern end of it there is Victoria Museum which houses a collection of old colonial era photos, entrance fee is included into Victoria Park's entrance ticket. Rs1000 (kids 500). (updated May 2025) 2 Nuwara Eliya Post Office. A picturesque Tudor-style, two-storey red brick building close to the big roundabout at the centre of town. One of the oldest post offices in Sri Lanka and still in use. It has a postcard and stamp collectors shop, which sells some recent first day covers, from 100Rs. (updated May 2025) 3 Lake Gregory (less than a mile from the centre of town). Large man-made lake, along the edge is a beautiful park, with water sports (paddle boats, jet ski rides and cruises) as well as other recreational activities. Offers a splendid and peaceful environment for sightseeing and boating. Boats can be hired from the area. Entrance to the Lake Gregory park Rs1000 (kids 500). (updated May 2025) 4 Hill Club. ...
[Do] Take a walk up through the tea plantations south-west of the town to the top of Single Tree Hill for a splendid view over Nuwara Eliya. From the hill top you can walk north for a couple of kilometres along the ridgetop to a nearby village and get a tuk-tuk/three-wheeler or walk back to town. Playing golf is also an option at 1 Nuwara Eliya Golf, along with heading to the 2 racecourses (the only proper ones in Sri Lanka). These are both traditions left over from the colonial era. Take a train trip from Nanu Oya towards Kandy. For the colonial experience book a 1st class ticket in the observation car. For an authentic local experience book a 3rd class ticket and hang out of the door of the carriage. Further afield: 3 Adam's Peak (There are regular buses from Hatton (railway connection, right behind the railway station in high season, Rs 200) or Maskeliya (Rs 100) to Dalhousie (Nallathanniya). (Maskeliya is also a good hub for the Gartmore Falls.) The peak can also be reached from the Ratnapura side, even though this trail goes through the jungle and is less favourable than the staircase from Dalhousie.). ...

# 3-day trip to Nuwara Eliya

A scenic 3-day Hill Country trip for a Sri Lankan family from Colombo to Nuwara Eliya, taking in tea estates, Single Tree Hill, town landmarks, and Lake Gregory.

**Starting point:** Colombo

*Weather:* 2026-11-23: dense drizzle; min 12.2 °C, max 20.6 °C; chance of precipitation 100%; rainfall 4.6 mm; max wind 5.4 km/h (Open-Meteo)

- **Afternoon: Nuwara Eliya Post Office** (about 1 h) - Visit the iconic two-storey Tudor-style red brick post office located in the town centre and check out the postcard and stamp shop. _(Wikivoyage)_
- **Afternoon: Victoria Park** (about 2 h) - Explore Victoria Park to view diverse flora ranging from tropical rain forest plants to English gardens, and visit Victoria Museum at the southern end. _(Wikivoyage)_
